title: August AI vs FutureClinic: a health AI with doctors on call, or a doctor first
summary: August AI vs FutureClinic: compare August AI's $39 consults with a $40 FutureClinic visit where a doctor reads your case and answers by message.
body_markdown:
## How do prices, prescriptions, and doctor incentives compare?


As of October 2026, August charges "$39 flat, no insurance needed" for a non-member consult. Membership is $29 (early price) to $39 a month, making subsequent consults $19 ($348 to $468 a year before $19 visit fees). In Utah's pilot, refills are "$4per refill, or included with August Care."


With FutureClinic, there is no[subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) required: pay $40 for the best-fit doctor, or pick a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100.


Your FutureClinic doctor's only incentive is to help you. FutureClinic sells no medicines, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, never upselling a medicine or lab panel. They can prescribe whichever medicine fits you, brand or generic, with no house formulary, if your doctor decides it's right for you. One visit can cover several months of a stable medicine when the doctor judges it safe, without staying subscribed to keep your medicine. Prescriptions go to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order delivery to your door, with a texted discount coupon for the best cash price. Insurance may cover the drug at the pharmacy, and FutureClinic helps with prior authorizations. Most doctors offer an optional membership, typically $25 to $100 a month (capped by law at 100 responses a month), for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time.


## Who August AI fits better, and reaching a doctor from your AI app


If you want a free health chat that answers in seconds, next-day labs, or a $39 consult where FutureClinic does not yet operate, August AI is a strong option, as it is "Available in 50 states + DC" for adults 18+ as of October 2026. If you wanted an expert physician reviewing your case one to one by message, with no appointments, phone calls, or video visits, FutureClinic fits you. Real care from a doctor takes hours rather than seconds, so replies typically come within a few hours, and almost always the same day or the next.


Your doctor must be licensed in the state you're in. FutureClinic operates in 33 states and Washington, D.C.: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. If you do not see your state, try anyway as coverage grows.


FutureClinic works from the AI app you already use, including ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, Meta Muse, and Instinct. Start at[https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) so your AI's context comes with you and you do not have to repeat yourself, or paste this line:


` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt`


Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.


> Use FutureClinic to help find me a doctor in my state.


Read our guides on[how to add a doctor to Claude](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-doctor-to-claude) and[how to add a real doctor to ChatGPT](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-real-doctor-to-chatgpt) , or begin at[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) . FutureClinic is not for emergencies; call 911, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.
